text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., under federal investigation for Medicare fraud, said late Friday that its chief financial officer has resigned.
The company said in a one-sentence statement that Robert Stearns, who was "hired by the previous management" on July 21, has resigned effective Aug. 31.

The news came a day after the nation's largest for-profit hospital chain said it will widen disclosure of its Medicare cost reports, impose a new review system on Medicare coding procedures and adopt a new regulatory compliance program.
Company officials were not immediately available to comment on Stearns' resignation.

Three Columbia managers were indicted on fraud charges last week, and the former chief executive and president were ousted on July 24 by a board of directors angry about the handling of the ongoing investigation.

The four-month-old probe by several federal agencies led last month to raids on 33 company facilities in six states and seizures of cartloads of documents pertaining to laboratory billing and home health care.

The company, moving to blunt the massive investigation, also said Thursday that it will stop paying cash incentive payments to employees and that it will sell or spin off its home health division, which has been a target of the probe.
The move to jettison the home health unit may remove a legal irritant but industry analysts said it could also hurt prospects for a $20 billion company that has expanded aggressively.
Shareholders have filed at least 11 lawsuits against Columbia, which is based in Nashville, and the attorneys general of Florida, Texas and Alabama are conducting their own investigations.
It was not clear if the company had appointed an interim chief financial officer or was searching for a successor.
Columbia's stock edged down 6 cents to close at $33.875 on the New York Stock Exchange before the announcement.
